# Jonah Chapter 3 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 340v–341r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/JON_003_page_001.jpg

---

**3:1** And-was the-word of-YHWH to Yonah a-second-time [shenit], saying: **3:2** "Arise [qum], go [lekh] to Nineveh, the-city the-great, and-call [qera] to-her the-calling [ha-qeri'ah] which I [am] speaking [dover] to-you."

**3:3** And-rose [vayyaqam] Yonah and-went [vayyyelekh] to Nineveh according-to-the-word of-YHWH. And-Nineveh was a-city great [gedolah] to-God [le-lohim] — a-journey [mahalakh] of-three days. **3:4** And-began [vayyachel] Yonah to-enter [lavo] the-city, a-journey of-one day, and-he-called [vayyiqra] and-said, "Yet [od] forty [arba'im] days and-Nineveh is-overthrown [nehpakhet]."

**3:5** And-believed [vayya'aminu] the-men [anshei] of-Nineveh in-God [be-lohim], and-they-called [vayyiqre'u] a-fast [tsom], and-put-on [vayyilbeshu] sackcloth [saqqim] from-their-greatest [mi-gedolam] to-their-least [ve-ad qetannam].

**3:6** And-the-word reached [vayyigga] the-king of-Nineveh, and-he-arose [vayyaqam] from-his-throne [kisso], and-removed [vayya'aver] his-robe [addarto] from-upon-him, and-covered [vayekhas] [himself with] sackcloth [saq] and-sat [vayyeshev] upon the-ashes [ha-efer].

**3:7** And-he-caused-to-be-proclaimed [vayyz'eq] and-said in-Nineveh, by-the-decree [mi-ta'am] of-the-king and-his-great-ones [gedolav], saying: "The-man [ha-adam] and-the-beast [ha-behemah], the-cattle [ha-baqar] and-the-flock [ha-tson] — let-them-not taste [yit'amu] anything [me'umah]; let-them-not graze [yir'u] and-water [mayim] let-them-not drink [yishtu]."

**3:8** "And-let-them-be-covered [veyitkassu] [with] sackcloth — the-man and-the-beast — and-let-them-call [veyiqre'u] to-God [el-elohim] with-strength [be-chozkah]; and-let-them-turn [veyashuvu] each [ish] from-his-evil [ra'ah] way [darkho] and-from the-violence [ha-chamas] which [is] in-their-hands [kappehem]."

**3:9** "Who knows [mi yode'a]? He-may-turn [yashuv] and-relent [venicham] the-God [ha-elohim], and-turn [veshav] from-the-burning [me-charon] of-his-anger [appo], and-we-will-not perish [noved]."

**3:10** And-saw [vayyar] the-God [ha-elohim] their-deeds [ma'asehem], that they-turned [shavu] from-their-evil [ra'ah] way [darkam]; and-the-God relented [vayyinnachem] concerning-the-evil [ha-ra'ah] which he-had-spoken [dibber] to-do [la'asot] to-them, and-he-did-not-do-it [lo asah].

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.3 — "great to God":** *Gedolah le-lohim* — literally "great to/for God." Some translations render this as a superlative ("exceedingly great"), understanding *le-lohim* as an intensifier. Others read it as "great to God" — important in God's eyes.

**v.4 — "overthrown":** *Nehpakhet* — the same root (*h-p-kh*, "to overturn") used for the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah (Gen 19:25). The word carries ambiguity: it can mean "destroyed" or "transformed/changed." Nineveh is indeed "overturned" — but by repentance, not by fire.

**v.9 — "Who knows?":** *Mi yode'a* — compare Joel 2:14 ("Who knows whether he will turn and relent?"). The king expresses genuine theological uncertainty — repentance is offered without any guarantee of success. The phrase preserves divine freedom.

**v.10 — "relented":** *Vayyinnachem* — from *nacham*, "to relent/be sorry/change one's mind." This verb when applied to God is theologically charged. Does God "change his mind"? The Hebrew allows for a view where God's response changes because the human situation has changed.

*— EMET*
